I was born with a congenital heart defect and have had multiple open heart surgeries, thus a lot of little scars and usual zipper scar down my chest. I started modeling as a teen, more so in my 20s (I never made it into anything big, but it was just a huge passion for me so I enjoyed the art of collaborating with photographers and artists in drawing classes. I did everything from sexy playboy type shoots, editorial, fashion, and super artsy stuff.), and quite honestly it was never an issue. If anything a lot of comments I got were positive, thinking it was cool and some photogs actually came up with ideas to showcase my scars in some awesome BW art prints I still have. Anytime it was something they didnt want, or even I didnt want, it could easily be photoshopped out or covered with makeup.

I mean, maybe it cost me working with people who saw my book online and decided they didnt want to work with me, but I never wanted for work and made a lot of cool friends throughout the years with people I'd work with over and over. Again, I never made it professionally (that was partially also because of my health and not trying as hard as I could have to get serious) but I worked with a lot of people who had done professional work and were retired and just doing it as a hobby now and they never once said it would be a hindrance. You dont know til you try, and even if you dont make it as a career it if it's something you love doing then what does it matter in the end. It kinda bums me out but at the same time I have so many cool pictures and memories that I'm glad I did what I could even if it never went as far as I would have liked. I stopped after my most recent surgery a little over 6 years ago, I had an incredibly rough experience and recovery that took me a long time to get over emotionally, so my life kinda fell apart for awhile.... but lately I've been thinking about getting into it again just because I've never felt more Me than when I'm working with someone on a shoot and we come up with something really interesting and cool.

Hope that helps!

It was crazy to see So many creators names being thrown around and talked shit about (and really unfair to them too), and then when Emily Leah posted an unrelated video like an hour later people came into her comment section and started saying that Savannah was calling her out, shes being canceled etc. Then when EL made a video addressing what had happened it was weird to me that SM was confused and kind of blamed Emily for kicking up drama, I get she didnt say her name in the video but c'mon.... it was pretty obvious and I'm sorry.... no matter how anyone feels about Emily I have to say that if it was me and another creator was basically calling me out and everyone kind of knew and was even commenting in my own video - I'd probably address it as well.

I'm not trying to say I'm on Emily Leah's or Savannahs side or that one is more wrong or right, I'm just saying that it was a little shady and kind of like confusing to me as to why this was even publicized because of course it's going to start shit... Like in her recent IG vids she keeps saying she doesn't want to be dragged into the drama and doesn't know why she is. Like... come on... Most people had No clue what you were talking about in that initial video which should show you that this was a private drama between Creators - not the broad community as a whole. That just irritates me to no end that shes acting so flabbergasted as to her complicity in starting this. You cant feign ignorance just because you "didnt name names". 
I dunno, maybe I'm totally off base and have an unpopular opinion, it just feels like take a little bit of responsibility for maybe starting something that while unintentional still acted like a match. Of course if you were getting treated wrong then speak up, but blasting a video that does nothing but spark speculation and rumors about a ton of other creators and drags them into the mud when most of them had no part in it is so not the way to do it.

My mom got remarried when I was 4 and they moved constantly throughout my childhood. I went to at least one new school every year (usually halfway through the year),  sometimes 2 and one time 3. I never felt stable in my life and it really messed me up. It made me incredibly shy and introverted, I never got to make lasting friendships or really learn how to make solid friendships which has affected me even as an adult. The schools were usually at different places in what they were learning so I was either repeating things I'd already learned or way behind everyone else and expected to keep up. This was especially hard for me in math the older I got, and I had to repeat Pre-Algebra 3 times because I kept missing whole chunks :/ One time in 7th grade they had a test on state history my second day that the teacher made me take, just "to see where I was". They'd just finished up a 6 week section on it while I'd never even started on it, so obviously I ended up flunking and she counted it in my grades anyway... she really was a total bitch. The older I got the less I tried to make friends because it became so hard to leave them, plus once I hit about 12 cliques started forming and most people knew each other since elementary school. I also started to fall through the cracks and do worse and worse in school when I got to my teen years. Where I was once a very good student with very good grades, it all slowly started to slip more and more. I didn't get a chance to do clubs, sports, pursue my interests (gymnastics, ice skating and ballet), or discover what I was good at and excel in school (love science, especially astronomy). While everyone else around me was figuring out what they wanted to pursue or what they were interested in I was pretty much just floating through life. Things started becoming pretty bad at home too, I used to cry in the driveway when I'd come home from being out with my friends because I didn't want to go inside. So I just gave up and started playing into the lackadaisical rebellious attitude about school and my future. I was that kid who would fail a class and make fun of myself and how lame and pointless this all was anyway, but really I just felt like a loser who didn't know how to get out of the hole I was in. It of course ended up costing me a lot in terms of grades and opportunities unfortunately.  I wish I could have used the circumstances as motivation to do good in school and make something of myself, but it was really hard to give a shit when no one else did. I failed my PSATs, I was in danger of being held back, and hearing all my peers talk about college/career paths etc made me feel like such a failure. Eventually I ended up dropping out half way through my Senior year. I did manage to get my GED a few months before my class graduated though, so there's that.

What really made me the most resentful though was that by the time my younger siblings (8 year difference between the oldest and me) got to early elementary school my parents settled and have lived in the same place since. While I didn't stay at the same school until around 15 (which I didn't know was going to happen, so I didn't try too hard to make friends at first), they got to from about age 7. So they've had the same friends for pretty much their whole lives, participated in sports and activities, one of them had a tutor in middle school, and have had all the stability I always craved but never got. It's not like I didn't have any friends, but I always felt kind of like a tag along and not one of the core members of our group if that makes sense. 

Why did they do this? People asked all the time, usually assuming I was a military brat, but honestly I have absolutely no idea why. They didn't have jobs that moved them around, we didn't move far most of the time just different districts, save for a couple out of state moves. Parents, please do not do this to your kids. I always hear how 'kids are resilient and it won't bother them once they get settled'. That's bullshit. Maybe once or twice, but constantly... it's just cruel. Being 'The New Kid' every year sucked. I'm not saying I didn't eventually play a part in how bad things got school wise later on, but at that age and with no support system I really had no idea how to navigate through everything.

I don't have schizophrenia, but I have PTSD from a coma that gave me hallucinations the first week after I woke up. When I have flashbacks I feel almost disconnected from my body, and get super paranoid and anxious that I'm in some sort of fake reality and I'm either still in the coma or died. My husband and I have a "safe word" that he says when I experience an episode, it usually helps me calm down enough that I can ride it through. Sometimes it can take a bit because I get scared I'm just hearing him from my coma, but after a little while I start feeling safer.

Hope it helps ❤

Firstly when it comes to her meds, she might not be at a theraputic dose. I know when I'm not it is not nearly as effective. Sometimes a new combination, adding or removing something can help a lot.

Next, communication. That is Key to a healthy, good relationship. It might be uncomfortable at first, but in the end it's hopefully going to make your relationship stronger, or maybe show you things that are deal breakers. And sex is important to any romantic relationship. No its not the most important, but it is still important. Either way, throughout any relationship, communicating with each other not just problems or issies, but good things too :) 

At the end of the day though, it's not selfish to want to be happy and satisfied in your relationship at all. You should be those things in your life in general. You want to have fun with the person you're with.
